tools_used: CourtListener MCP: search, call_endpoint (dockets), get_endpoint_item (clusters), search_document
engine web search / fetch (supremecourt.gov docket pages and an order list PDF)
helpful: Full provisioned petition text: it named the companion and related dockets (26-159, 26-263, 25-213) that drove the forecast
The salience-band Term table with bracketed reached rates made the arrival anchor a one-step pooled computation
supremecourt.gov docket pages (via web fetch) supplied the response-requested / amici / relist history of the direct prior and the state of the three related petitions
CourtListener cluster lookup confirmed the decision below and its unanimity
gaps: CourtListener's docket index holds no SCOTUS dockets for any of the five numbers checked, so related-docket state had to come from supremecourt.gov via generic web fetch; a sanctioned supremecourt.gov docket fetch tool for a named docket number would replace six web calls
fedcourts query has no docket-number or case-name filter, so a known prior (Atlas Turner, 25-213) could not be pulled as a corpus row; two 400-500 row scans by name found nothing
No statpack cut for petitions with a response-requested prior on the same issue, or for interlocutory state-court petitions (finality), both of which moved this forecast
Web-search summaries can misattribute order-list notations across adjacent entries; verifying against the PDF text cost an extra call and was necessary
notes: About 27 retrieval calls (5 corpus, 12 MCP, 11 web), slightly over the advisory 25; the overage went to verifying a wrong web-summary claim about a would-grant notation.
